title_en: Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Tort Liability Part of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en:
Article 21 Where a motor vehicle that has not been insured with compulsory insurance according to law causes damage in a traffic accident, and the person obliged to purchase the insurance and the person liable for the traffic accident are not the same person, and the infringed party jointly claims tort liability against both the person obliged to purchase the insurance and the person liable for the traffic accident, the person liable for the traffic accident shall bear all the liability that the tortfeasor should bear; the person obliged to purchase the insurance shall bear liability jointly with the person liable for the traffic accident within the limits of the liability amount of the motor vehicle compulsory insurance, provided that the total compensation actually paid by the liable parties shall not exceed the amount of loss that the infringed party is entitled to receive.
Where the person obliged to purchase the insurance pays compensation in advance and subsequently seeks recourse from the person liable for the traffic accident for the portion exceeding the limits of the motor vehicle compulsory insurance liability, the People's Court shall support such claim.

Article 22 Where a motor vehicle driver, after leaving the vehicle, suffers damage caused by being hit or run over by the vehicle due to the driver's own fault, such as failing to take braking measures, and the driver requests the insurer of the motor vehicle compulsory insurance to compensate within the limits of the compulsory insurance liability, or requests the insurer of the motor vehicle commercial third-party liability insurance to compensate in accordance with the insurance contract, the People's Court shall not support such claim; however, the corresponding compensation claim may be supported in accordance with the relevant provisions of the motor vehicle occupant liability insurance.

Article 23 Where a dangerous animal, such as a ferocious dog, the keeping of which is prohibited, causes damage to another person, and the animal keeper or manager claims exemption from liability or mitigation of liability, the People's Court shall not support such claim.

Article 24 Where a property service enterprise or other building manager fails to take necessary safety and security measures to prevent objects thrown from a building or objects falling from a building from causing damage to another person, and the specific tortfeasor and the property service enterprise or other building manager are named as co-defendants, the People's Court shall, in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 1198 and Article 1254 of the Civil Code, specify in the judgment that the property service enterprise or other building manager that has failed to take necessary safety and security measures shall bear supplementary liability commensurate with its fault, to the extent that the obligor is still unable to perform after the People's Court has enforced execution against the property of the specific tortfeasor according to law.

Article 25 Where a property service enterprise or other building manager fails to take necessary safety and security measures to prevent objects thrown from a building or objects falling from a building from causing damage to another person, and after investigation by the public security or other authorities, it remains difficult to ascertain the specific tortfeasor before the conclusion of the court debate in the first instance of the civil case, the property service enterprise or other building manager that has failed to take necessary safety and security measures shall bear liability commensurate with its fault. The remaining damage to the infringed party shall be appropriately compensated by the building users who may have caused the harm.
After the specific tortfeasor is identified, where the property service enterprise or other building manager that has already borne liability, or the building users who may have caused the harm, seek recourse against the specific tortfeasor, the People's Court shall support such claim in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 1198 and paragraph 1 of Article 1254 of the Civil Code.

Article 26 This Interpretation shall come into force on September 27, 2024.
After the coming into force of this Interpretation, cases of first instance and second instance that have not yet been finally adjudicated by the People's Court shall be governed by this Interpretation. Where a final judgment has been rendered before the coming into force of this Interpretation, and a party applies for retrial or a retrial is decided in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, the laws and judicial interpretations in effect at that time shall apply.
